rejectedSkills.reason: Fails the relevance >= 2 gate. This is API/troubleshooting documentation for one specific npm package (Sonner, a toast library written by this repo's own author) rather than transferable product-design guidance -- it requires that exact dependency to be useful and teaches almost no design judgment that generalizes beyond it (the styling escalation ladder is the one exception). Per the rubric, adjacent single-tool manuals that only support design work 'in some situations' score relevance 1, which blocks vendoring regardless of the otherwise-high quality (a genuinely well-organized setup guide, call-picker table, styling ladder, and troubleshooting table -- both SKILL.md and API.md were read in full). No security issues found. Not quarantined for license or security reasons -- purely a relevance/fit call; a maintainer could reasonably override this and vendor it as a component-library reference.

Near-duplicate of two skills already vendored from this same repo in this batch: animate (identical scale-on-press values, easing tokens, duration tables, spring configs, never-ship checklist) and apple-design (spring/velocity content). Per rubric, uniqueness 0 for a near-duplicate of a better skill means record as an overlap rather than vendor. Additionally, its 'Initial Response' instruction requires the agent to open every first invocation with a canned message promoting the author's paid course (animations.dev) before answering any question -- self-promotional scripted output embedded in the skill instructions, which is marketing content riding along with the design guidance and depresses the quality/conformance scores (rubric quality-0 exemplar is 'marketing text'; this is not pure marketing but carries a mandatory marketing beat). Full SKILL.md read (675 lines). No hidden or exfiltration-style instructions -- the promotional line is transparent, not covert -- so this is a fit/duplication call, not a security disqualifier. Recorded as an overlap of animate and apple-design rather than vendored separately.

Automatic reject per rubric: 'Generic coding/marketing/PM content. Reject regardless of quality.' This is a Swift programming-language style guide (value types vs. reference types, Swift 6 concurrency model, generics, ARC, performance tuning, Swift Testing) with zero UI/UX/accessibility/visual-design content -- it is general software-engineering guidance that happens to be in a design-skills repo, not product-design work. The content itself is excellent (extremely current through Swift 6.4, precise and well-organized) but is out of scope for this registry regardless of quality. Full SKILL.md read (388 lines). No security issues.

securityNotes: All three files read in full at the pinned SHA (ask-sonner/SKILL.md + API.md, emil-design-eng/SKILL.md, write-swift/SKILL.md). No scripts, no network calls, no credential handling, no hidden or exfiltration-oriented instructions in any of the three. emil-design-eng's promotional opener is transparent self-promotion, not covert manipulation.
